NetSentinel - End User Licence Agreement (short form)

Copyright (c) 2026. All rights reserved.

1. LICENCE. You may install and use NetSentinel on computers that you own or are
   authorised to administer. One installation per site is the intended model; there is
   no per-device limit.

2. PERMITTED USE. Network discovery, monitoring, alerting and remote-session launching
   are permitted only on networks you own or have written authority to administer.
   Scanning networks you do not control may be illegal in your jurisdiction.

3. NO WARRANTY. The software is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind. It is an
   aid to an administrator, not a substitute for one: a diagnosis, a device
   classification or an availability figure can be wrong, and you must verify anything
   you act on.

4. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors are not
   liable for any indirect, incidental or consequential loss, including lost profits,
   lost data or business interruption, arising from use of the software.

5. DATA. The software runs on your own infrastructure. It contacts only: the public-IP
   lookup services, the identity provider you configure, your SMTP/SIEM/Slack/Teams
   endpoints, and any update or vendor-list URL you configure. No telemetry is sent to
   the authors.

6. THIRD-PARTY COMPONENTS. The optional packages (cryptography, scapy, psutil) keep their
   own licences; see sbom.json. The Python standard library is used under the PSF licence.

7. TERMINATION. This licence ends if you breach it. Uninstall with uninstall.cmd.

8. NO SUPPORT OBLIGATION unless a separate written support agreement exists.

Replace this file with your own agreement before distributing the software to third
parties; this short form is a starting point, not legal advice.
